title: 2 Kings Chapter 17 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 17 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 17 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 17.

questions.question: In which year of Ahaz king of Judah did Hoshea begin to reign over Israel in Samaria?
options: The twelfth year
The ninth year
The first year
The fifteenth year
questions.correctAnswer: The twelfth year
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:1 states that Hoshea began to reign in the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah.

questions.question: How long did Hoshea reign as king over Israel?
options: Nine years
Twelve years
Three years
Seven years
questions.correctAnswer: Nine years
questions.explanation: According to 2 Kings 17:1, Hoshea reigned over Israel for nine years.

questions.question: What kind of deeds did Hoshea do in the sight of the LORD?
options: He did evil, but not like the kings before him
He did good and followed the LORD
He did no evil at all
He did worse than all kings before him
questions.correctAnswer: He did evil, but not like the kings before him
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:2 says Hoshea did evil in the sight of the LORD, but not as the kings of Israel before him.

questions.question: Who came against Hoshea king of Israel, leading Hoshea to become his servant?
options: Shalmaneser king of Assyria
So king of Egypt
Jeroboam son of Nebat
Pharaoh king of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Shalmaneser king of Assyria
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:3 tells us that Shalmaneser king of Assyria came against Hoshea, who then became his servant.

questions.question: Why did the king of Assyria imprison Hoshea?
options: Because Hoshea conspired by sending messengers to the king of Egypt and did not give tribute
Because Hoshea rebelled openly in battle
Because Hoshea refused to pay any tribute at all
Because Hoshea fled to Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Because Hoshea conspired by sending messengers to the king of Egypt and did not give tribute
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:4 explains that the king of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea when he sent messengers to Egypt and did not give tribute as before, so he was imprisoned.

questions.question: How long did the king of Assyria besiege Samaria?
options: Three years
One year
Nine years
Seven years
questions.correctAnswer: Three years
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:5 states that the king of Assyria besieged Samaria for three years.

questions.question: What happened to Israel in the ninth year of Hoshea's reign?
options: The king of Assyria took Samaria and carried Israel away into Assyria
Hoshea defeated the Assyrian army
Samaria was freed from siege
Israel made peace with Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: The king of Assyria took Samaria and carried Israel away into Assyria
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:6 records that in the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria took Samaria and exiled Israel into Assyria.

questions.question: Why did the children of Israel sin against the LORD according to 2 Kings 17?
options: They feared other gods and walked in the statutes of the heathen
They were afraid of the king of Assyria
They followed only the laws of Moses
They worshipped only the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They feared other gods and walked in the statutes of the heathen
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:7-8 explains that Israel sinned by fearing other gods and walking in the statutes of the heathen.

questions.question: Where did the children of Israel build high places and set up images?
options: In all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fenced city
Only in Jerusalem
In the desert only
Only in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: In all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fenced city
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:9 states that Israel built high places in all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fenced city.

questions.question: What did the children of Israel burn in all the high places?
options: Incense
Olive oil
Water
Grain
questions.correctAnswer: Incense
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:11 tells that they burnt incense in all the high places.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD commanded Israel not to serve idols, but they served them anyway.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:12 clearly states that the LORD said not to serve idols, yet Israel served them.

questions.question: True or False: The prophets and seers testified against Israel and Judah, calling them to turn from evil ways.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: According to 2 Kings 17:13, the LORD testified by prophets and seers to turn from evil and keep commandments.

questions.question: True or False: Israel obeyed the LORD’s commands after the prophets’ warnings.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:14 states they would not hear but hardened their necks, disbelieving the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Israel rejected the LORD’s statutes and followed the heathen nations around them.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:15 says they rejected the LORD’s statutes and followed vanity like the heathen, so the statement is true. But since the question says 'True or False: Israel rejected the LORD’s statutes and followed the heathen nations', the answer is True. Correction: The question states they rejected statutes and followed heathen, which is true, so the correct answer is True.

questions.question: In 2 Kings 17, which event comes first?
options: Hoshea becomes king of Israel
The king of Assyria besieges Samaria for three years
Israel is carried away into Assyria
Hoshea is imprisoned by the king of Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: Hoshea becomes king of Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:1 records Hoshea beginning to reign before the siege and imprisonment mentioned in later verses.

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 17 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 17 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 17:15, what did the children of Israel reject that led them to follow vain things and the heathen around them?
options: God's statutes, covenant, and testimonies
The kings of Assyria
The prophets' warnings
The laws of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: God's statutes, covenant, and testimonies
questions.explanation: Verse 15 states that Israel rejected God's statutes, covenant, and testimonies, which caused them to follow vanity and the heathen. This rejection led to their downfall as described in verses 15 and 16.

questions.question: How did the children of Israel defy the commandments of the LORD as described in 2 Kings 17:16?
options: By making molten images, calves, groves, and serving Baal
By building altars only in Jerusalem
By fasting and praying excessively
By worshipping only the host of heaven
questions.correctAnswer: By making molten images, calves, groves, and serving Baal
questions.explanation: Verse 16 clearly describes how Israel left all commandments and made molten images, two calves, groves, and worshipped Baal, indicating their disobedience.

questions.question: What severe actions did Israel commit involving their children as stated in 2 Kings 17:17?
options: Passing them through fire, practicing divination, enchantments, and selling themselves to evil
Sending them to foreign lands as captives
Educating them in the laws of the LORD
Building schools for their children
questions.correctAnswer: Passing them through fire, practicing divination, enchantments, and selling themselves to evil
questions.explanation: Verse 17 highlights the evil practices of Israel, including causing their sons and daughters to pass through fire and using divination and enchantments, provoking the LORD to anger.

questions.question: What was the LORD's reaction to Israel's sins and disobedience as described in 2 Kings 17:18?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 18 states that the LORD was very angry with Israel and removed them out of His sight, leaving only the tribe of Judah.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 17:19, did Judah keep the commandments of the LORD their God?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 19 explains that Judah also did not keep the commandments of the LORD but walked according to the statutes of Israel, which they made themselves.

questions.question: What happened to the seed of Israel according to 2 Kings 17:20 because of their rebellion?
options: They were rejected, afflicted, and delivered into the hand of spoilers until cast out
They prospered and multiplied
They were given special protection
They returned to Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: They were rejected, afflicted, and delivered into the hand of spoilers until cast out
questions.explanation: Verse 20 clearly states that the LORD rejected all the seed of Israel, afflicted them, and delivered them into the hand of spoilers until He cast them out of His sight.

questions.question: How did Jeroboam influence Israel according to 2 Kings 17:21?
options: He drove Israel from following the LORD and caused them to sin greatly
He led Israel back to the LORD
He united Israel and Judah
He expanded Israel's borders peacefully
questions.correctAnswer: He drove Israel from following the LORD and caused them to sin greatly
questions.explanation: Verse 21 states that Jeroboam was made king and caused Israel to sin a great sin by driving them away from following the LORD.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 17:22, how did the children of Israel respond to Jeroboam's sins?
options: They walked in all his sins and did not depart from them
They immediately repented and returned to the LORD
They replaced Jeroboam with a new king
They migrated to other lands
questions.correctAnswer: They walked in all his sins and did not depart from them
questions.explanation: Verse 22 explains that Israel continued in all the sins of Jeroboam, never departing from them.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 17:23 say was the fulfillment of the LORD's word spoken through the prophets?
options: Israel was carried away from their land into Assyria
Israel defeated Assyria in battle
Israel built new cities in Samaria
Israel expanded their territory
questions.correctAnswer: Israel was carried away from their land into Assyria
questions.explanation: Verse 23 confirms that the LORD removed Israel from His sight as prophesied and carried them away to Assyria.

questions.question: What did the king of Assyria do with the people from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath, and Sepharvaim as described in 2 Kings 17:24?
options: Placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel
Sent them back to their homelands
Forced them into slavery in Egypt
Made them servants of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 24 explains that the Assyrian king settled these nations in Samaria to replace Israel and they dwelt in its cities.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 17:25, why did the LORD send lions among the nations placed in Samaria?
options: Because they feared not the LORD
Because they rebelled against the king of Assyria
Because they refused to build altars
Because they worshipped only the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Because they feared not the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 25 states that the people feared not the LORD, so He sent lions which killed some of them.

questions.question: What concern did the nations in Samaria express to the king of Assyria due to the lions, according to 2 Kings 17:26?
options: They did not know the manner of the God of the land
They wanted to return to Babylon
They asked for weapons to defend themselves
They sought to build new temples
questions.correctAnswer: They did not know the manner of the God of the land
questions.explanation: Verse 26 reveals that the nations explained to the Assyrian king that the lions killed them because they did not know how to fear the God of the land.

questions.question: What was the king of Assyria's solution to the lion problem among the nations in Samaria, according to 2 Kings 17:27?
options: Send a priest from Israel to teach them the manner of the God of the land
Send more soldiers to protect them
Remove the lions by hunting them
Relocate the nations elsewhere
questions.correctAnswer: Send a priest from Israel to teach them the manner of the God of the land
questions.explanation: Verse 27 shows the king commanded that a priest be sent to teach the people how to fear the God of the land to stop the lions.

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 17:28 illustrate the effect of the priest sent from Israel on the nations in Samaria?
options: The priest dwelt in Bethel and taught them to fear the LORD
The priest was rejected and expelled
The priest built an altar to Baal
The priest led a rebellion against Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: The priest dwelt in Bethel and taught them to fear the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 28 indicates that one of the priests taken from Samaria dwelt in Bethel and taught the people how to fear the LORD.

questions.question: Context question: What does 2 Kings 17:26 promise will happen if the nations placed in Samaria do what 2 Kings 17:27 instructs?
options: The lions will stop killing them because they learn the manner of the God of the land
They will be defeated by the Assyrian army
They will abandon their gods and worship Baal
They will build high places for their gods
questions.correctAnswer: The lions will stop killing them because they learn the manner of the God of the land
questions.explanation: Verse 26 explains the lions kill them because they do not know how to fear God. Verse 27 instructs sending a priest to teach the way of God, implying the lions will cease their attack once they learn.

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 17 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 17.

questions.question: Which gods did the men of Hamath make according to 2 Kings 17?
options: Ashima
Nergal
Succothbenoth
Adrammelech
questions.correctAnswer: Ashima
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:30 states that the men of Hamath made Ashima as their god.

questions.question: What did the Sepharvites do to their children as part of their worship?
options: Burnt them in fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech
Sacrificed them to Baal
Offered them as peace offerings
Dedicated them to the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: Burnt them in fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:31 describes that the Sepharvites burnt their children in fire to the gods Adrammelech and Anammelech.

questions.question: How did the nations placed in Samaria by the king of Assyria worship God according to their customs?
options: They feared the LORD and served their own gods
They abandoned all their gods and worshiped only the LORD
They destroyed all the graven images
They only worshiped the LORD without idols
questions.correctAnswer: They feared the LORD and served their own gods
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:33 explains that these nations feared the LORD but served their own gods according to their customs.

questions.question: What commandment did the LORD give regarding other gods in His covenant with Israel?
options: Ye shall not fear other gods, nor bow yourselves to them, nor serve them, nor sacrifice to them
Ye shall fear other gods alongside the LORD
Ye shall sacrifice to all gods to keep peace
Ye shall respect but not worship other gods
questions.correctAnswer: Ye shall not fear other gods, nor bow yourselves to them, nor serve them, nor sacrifice to them
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:35 records the LORD's covenant command forbidding the fear, bowing, serving, or sacrificing to other gods.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word 'grove' as used in 2 Kings 17:10, and what does it signify in the context?
options: A sacred tree or wooden idol used in pagan worship
A natural forest used for assemblies
A type of altar for burnt offerings
A fortified city or stronghold
questions.correctAnswer: A sacred tree or wooden idol used in pagan worship
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word often translated as 'grove' (Asherah) refers to a wooden cultic object or sacred tree used in idol worship, as noted in 2 Kings 17:10's context of idolatry.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in 2 Kings 17:35-39 to emphasize the covenant relationship between the LORD and Israel?
options: Inclusio framing the commands about fearing only the LORD
Chiasm highlighting the rejection of other gods
Parallelism contrasting obedience and disobedience
Foreshadowing of exile and restoration
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio framing the commands about fearing only the LORD
questions.explanation: Verses 35-39 use inclusio by repeating the theme of fearing only the LORD and not other gods, framing the covenant obligations clearly.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 17:41, what ongoing behavior did the nations in Samaria exhibit?
options: They feared the LORD and served their graven images just as their ancestors did
They fully abandoned idolatry and worshiped only the LORD
They destroyed all high places and idols
They returned to worship of the God of Israel exclusively
questions.correctAnswer: They feared the LORD and served their graven images just as their ancestors did
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:41 explains that these nations continued fearing the LORD but also served their graven images like their fathers had done.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage also emphasizes the prohibition against worshiping other gods as found in 2 Kings 17?
options: Exodus 20:3 - 'Thou shalt have no other gods before me'
Genesis 1:1 - God created the heavens and the earth
Psalms 23:1 - The Lord is my shepherd
Isaiah 53:5 - The suffering servant
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 20:3 - 'Thou shalt have no other gods before me'
questions.explanation: The command in 2 Kings 17:35 about not fearing or serving other gods echoes the first commandment found in Exodus 20:3.

questions.question: What reason does 2 Kings 17:26 give for the lions being sent among the nations settled in Samaria?
options: They did not know the manner of the God of the land
They worshiped the LORD exclusively
They built altars to the LORD
They were faithful to the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: They did not know the manner of the God of the land
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:26 states that the nations feared not the LORD properly because they did not know His ways, which led to lions being sent among them.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Kings 17:40, the nations in Samaria hearkened to the LORD and followed His statutes faithfully.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:40 clearly states that they did not hearken but did according to their former manner, disobeying the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: The chapter 2 Kings 17 shows a typology where the exile of Israel prefigures the later exile of Judah described in Jeremiah and Ezekiel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The exile of Israel in 2 Kings 17 foreshadows the exile of Judah later described in Jeremiah and Ezekiel, showing a biblical typology of judgment and restoration.

questions.question: Which king of Assyria is mentioned in 2 Kings 17 as the conqueror who took Samaria?
options: Shalmaneser
Sargon
Tiglath-Pileser
Esarhaddon
questions.correctAnswer: Shalmaneser
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:3 states that Shalmaneser king of Assyria came against Hoshea and later took Samaria.

questions.question: What was the consequence of Israel's sins against the LORD as described in 2 Kings 17:18?
options: The LORD was very angry and removed them out of his sight, leaving only Judah
They were blessed with peace and prosperity
They were given new land to settle
They entered into a new covenant with God
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD was very angry and removed them out of his sight, leaving only Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:18 describes the LORD's anger resulting in removal of Israel from his sight, sparing only the tribe of Judah.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 17, what role did the priests taken from Samaria play among the new nations settled there?
options: They taught the people the manner of the God of the land
They led a revolt against Assyria
They abandoned their duties and worshiped idols
They fled to Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: They taught the people the manner of the God of the land
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:27-28 explains that the king of Assyria commanded priests from Samaria to dwell among the new settlers to teach them how to fear the LORD.

questions.question: Which sin of Jeroboam is highlighted as causing Israel to depart from following the LORD in 2 Kings 17?
options: Leading Israel into great sin by instituting idol worship
Building the temple in Jerusalem
Destroying the high places of worship
Obeying the prophets
questions.correctAnswer: Leading Israel into great sin by instituting idol worship
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:21-22 states that Jeroboam made Israel sin greatly by leading them away from the LORD through idol worship.

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 17 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 17 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 17:1, during whose reign in Judah did Hoshea begin to reign over Israel?
options: Ahaz
Hezekiah
Jeroboam
Pekah
questions.correctAnswer: Ahaz
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:1 states that Hoshea began to reign over Israel in the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah.

questions.question: What specific sin of Israel led to their exile as described in 2 Kings 17:7-8?
options: They feared other gods and walked in the statutes of heathen nations.
They refused to pay tribute to Assyria.
They built the temple without God's approval.
They oppressed the poor and widows.
questions.correctAnswer: They feared other gods and walked in the statutes of heathen nations.
questions.explanation: Verses 7-8 explain that Israel sinned by fearing other gods and following the statutes of the heathen, which God had cast out before them.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 17:13 reveal about God's method of calling Israel to repentance?
options: God sent prophets and seers to testify against Israel and Judah.
God sent angels to punish Israel immediately.
God remained silent to test Israel's faith.
God performed miracles without warning.
questions.correctAnswer: God sent prophets and seers to testify against Israel and Judah.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:13 states that the LORD testified against Israel and Judah by all the prophets and seers, urging them to turn from evil and keep His commandments.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in 2 Kings 17:18 when the LORD removes Israel out of His sight because of their sin?
options: God’s holiness and justice
God’s omnipotence
God’s mercy and grace
God’s omnipresence
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness and justice
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 17:18, God’s holiness and justice are shown as He removes Israel due to their persistent sinfulness, demonstrating that He cannot tolerate sin unpunished.

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 17:22 describe Israel’s response to Jeroboam’s sins?
options: They walked in all the sins of Jeroboam and did not depart from them.
They immediately repented and returned to the LORD.
They were divided in their loyalties.
They followed only some of Jeroboam’s practices.
questions.correctAnswer: They walked in all the sins of Jeroboam and did not depart from them.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:22 states that the children of Israel continued in all the sins of Jeroboam and did not depart from them, showing persistent rebellion.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is highlighted by the exile of Israel in 2 Kings 17:6 and the cause given in 17:7-8?
options: God’s covenantal judgment for sin
The doctrine of predestination
The immanence of God in creation
The doctrine of angels and demons
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenantal judgment for sin
questions.explanation: Verses 6-8 show that Israel was exiled because of their covenantal unfaithfulness—sinning against the LORD who brought them out of Egypt—demonstrating the doctrine of God's covenantal judgment.

questions.question: 2 Kings 17:25-27 describes the sending of a priest to teach the new inhabitants the 'manner of the God of the land.' What does this reveal about God's providence?
options: God’s providential care extends even over foreign peoples in the land.
God abandons the land once Israel is exiled.
God only cares about Israel and ignores other nations.
God’s providence is limited to the temple worship.
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providential care extends even over foreign peoples in the land.
questions.explanation: The king of Assyria commanded a priest to be sent to teach the new inhabitants the fear of the LORD (17:27), showing God's providential governance even over foreign nations placed in Israel’s land.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do 2 Kings 17:35-39 convey about the exclusivity of worship and covenant relationship with God?
options: Only the LORD God, who delivered Israel from Egypt, is to be feared and worshipped, with exclusive covenantal loyalty.
God permits worship of multiple gods along with Him.
Worship is optional and does not affect covenant status.
The covenant includes worship of local gods alongside the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: Only the LORD God, who delivered Israel from Egypt, is to be feared and worshipped, with exclusive covenantal loyalty.
questions.explanation: Verses 35-39 emphasize the exclusive worship of the LORD who brought Israel out of Egypt and the requirement to keep His covenant and statutes without fearing other gods.

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 17:16 illustrate the human tendency towards idolatry despite God's clear commandments?
options: They made molten images, calves, groves, and served Baal, violating God's commandments.
They remained faithful to God and rejected all idols.
They worshiped only in the temple in Jerusalem.
They destroyed all idols in the land.
questions.correctAnswer: They made molten images, calves, groves, and served Baal, violating God's commandments.
questions.explanation: In verse 16, Israel abandoned God's commandments by creating idols and worshipping Baal, demonstrating human rebellion and idolatrous tendencies.

questions.question: What is the significance of the three-year siege mentioned in 2 Kings 17:5 in the broader narrative of Israel’s judgment?
options: It signifies the prolonged judgment and inevitability of exile due to persistent sin.
It was a brief, insignificant conflict.
It resulted in Israel’s victory and independence.
It was a test of Assyria’s military power only.
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies the prolonged judgment and inevitability of exile due to persistent sin.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:5 describes a three-year siege, underscoring God's prolonged judgment on Israel culminating in exile because of their unrepentant sinfulness.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 17:24-29, how did the introduction of foreign peoples and their gods affect the religious landscape of Samaria?
options: It led to syncretism where the LORD was feared alongside idol worship.
It caused the complete abandonment of all gods including the LORD.
It resulted in monotheistic worship of the LORD alone.
It brought peace and unity under one religion.
questions.correctAnswer: It led to syncretism where the LORD was feared alongside idol worship.
questions.explanation: Verses 24-29 reveal that the foreign peoples feared the LORD but also served their own gods, resulting in syncretism where multiple deities were worshipped simultaneously.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's covenant faithfulness is emphasized by the fact that Israel’s exile was 'as the LORD had said by all his servants the prophets' in 2 Kings 17:23?
options: God’s faithfulness to His word and prophetic warnings
God’s unpredictability in judgment
God’s disregard for prophecy
God’s selective memory regarding covenant
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness to His word and prophetic warnings
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17:23 confirms that Israel's exile fulfilled God's prophetic warnings, demonstrating His unchanging faithfulness to His word and covenantal justice.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the punishment of Israel was arbitrary and unjust. What does 2 Kings 17:7-18 actually teach about the reason and justice of Israel’s exile?
options: Israel’s exile was due to persistent sin and rejection of God’s covenant, reflecting divine justice.
Israel was exiled randomly without cause.
God punished Israel because of political weakness only.
Exile was a myth and never happened.
questions.correctAnswer: Israel’s exile was due to persistent sin and rejection of God’s covenant, reflecting divine justice.
questions.explanation: Verses 7-18 clearly state that Israel sinned by idolatry and rejecting God's laws, provoking His anger, and thus justly facing exile, disproving claims of arbitrariness.

questions.question: How does the narrative in 2 Kings 17:19-21 about Judah’s failure and Israel’s division contribute to our understanding of human sin and divine judgment?
options: It shows that both Israel and Judah repeatedly rejected God’s statutes, leading to division and judgment.
It shows Judah was blameless and always obeyed God.
It indicates that division was caused by foreign nations only.
It suggests that sin had no consequences for Israel or Judah.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that both Israel and Judah repeatedly rejected God’s statutes, leading to division and judgment.
questions.explanation: Verses 19-21 explain Judah’s failure to keep God’s commandments and the resulting division from David’s house, illustrating the pervasive nature of sin and its consequences.

questions.question: What combined truth about human sin and God’s patience can be drawn from 2 Kings 17:14 and 17:40?
options: Despite repeated warnings and hardening of hearts, Israel persisted in sinning in their former manner.
Israel repented quickly after the first warning.
God immediately destroyed Israel after their first sin.
Israel never sinned and remained faithful.
questions.correctAnswer: Despite repeated warnings and hardening of hearts, Israel persisted in sinning in their former manner.
questions.explanation: Verse 14 describes Israel’s hard neck and refusal to believe despite warnings; verse 40 shows they continued in their sinful ways, demonstrating human stubbornness and God’s long-suffering patience.
